compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The bridge project mapping (`.bridge_state/projects.json` — mapped keys + `legacy_default`)
can hold syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent or bot-invisible Jira project keys. Ticket F adds
SYNTACTIC write-time validation only (deliberately: a live call in the `set_project` write path
couples a local config write to Jira availability/auth, adds latency/flakiness, blocks legitimate
bootstrapping/provisioning order, and is TOCTOU-insufficient anyway). Ticket D adds an at-pass-time
EXISTENCE/visibility preflight inside the reconcile pass (the authoritative mutation guard).

Neither gives an operator an on-demand, non-blocking way to ask "are my mapped keys + legacy_default
actually visible to the bot right now?" outside a full reconcile pass. The projects.json corruption
incident (bug 05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27) would have been caught immediately by such a diagnostic.

## Scope (approved: additive diagnostic on the BRIDGE surface only)

Add an OPT-IN, credential-conditional, READ-ONLY, ADVISORY live mapped-key/legacy_default visibility
check to the existing `rebar bridge fsck` verb.

Hard constraints (separation of concerns — Jira stays an optional extra):
1. Live check lives ONLY on the bridge surface. Do NOT add it to core `rebar doctor`
   (`src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`) — that command is store/tracker health and MUST stay Jira-free
   (no reconciler / `[agents]` optional-extra import from core doctor).
2. Do NOT introduce a `bridge doctor` verb (epic 2f79 deliberately declined it — reuse `bridge fsck`).
3. Reuse D's mapped-project visibility helper — ONE shared helper answers "are the mapped keys +
   legacy_default visible to the bot?". Do NOT hand-roll a second Jira existence check (that is the
   duplicated-existence-check parity smell this epic has been eliminating). This is why G depends_on D.
4. Credential-conditional graceful degradation: when live Jira credentials are absent/incomplete,
   the step MUST skip cleanly (advisory "skipped — no live credentials"), NOT fail. Reuse the existing
   `run_access_check` (`access_check.py`) `missing_credentials` contract as the degradation pattern.
5. Read-only: no Jira writes; no bridge-state mutation. Advisory: the new step reports drift; it does
   NOT change `bridge fsck`'s existing pass/fail exit contract unless the maintainer explicitly wants a
   distinct advisory line (default: report-only, exit unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria

- `rebar bridge fsck` gains a mapped-project live-visibility step that, WHEN live creds are present,
  lists each mapped key + legacy_default and reports visible / NOT-visible-to-bot per the shared helper.
- WHEN live creds are absent/incomplete, the step degrades to an advisory "skipped (no live
  credentials)" and `bridge fsck` behaves exactly as today (no crash, exit contract unchanged).
- The visibility logic is the SAME helper D uses (no duplicate existence check); verified by test.
- Core `rebar doctor` imports remain Jira-free (no new reconciler/`[agents]` import reachable from
  `_commands/doctor.py`); verified by test/inspection.
- Always-on unit tests: (a) creds-present path reports a seeded invisible key; (b) creds-absent path
  skips gracefully; (c) core-doctor-stays-Jira-free assertion. RED→GREEN.

## Notes
- Depends on D for the shared visibility helper. Do not start until D's helper shape is landed/known.
- Same workflow as A/B/D: fresh worktree off origin/main, review-plan → sign-review → claim, RED→GREEN
  TDD, make lint/typecheck + targeted pytest, commit -s with rebar-ticket trailer, push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main.
